title: The North Wind and the Sun
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A dispute arose between the North Wind and the Sun, each claiming that he was stronger than the other. At last they agreed to try their powers upon a traveller, to see which could soonest strip him of his cloak. The North Wind had the first try; and, gathering up all his force for the attack, he came whirling furiously down upon the man, and caught up his cloak as though he would wrest it from him by one single effort: but the harder he blew, the more closely the man wrapped it round himself. Then came the turn of the Sun. At first he beamed gently upon the traveller, who soon unclasped his cloak and walked on with it hanging loosely about his shoulders: then he shone forth in his full strength, and the man, before he had gone many steps, was glad to throw his cloak right off and complete his journey more lightly clad.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the North Wind and the Sun disagree about?
options: Which of them rises first
Which of them the traveller likes best
Which of them is stronger
Which of them can travel faster

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the North Wind and the Sun agree to test on the traveller?
options: Which could soonest strip him of his cloak
Which could make him walk fastest
Which could make him fall asleep
Which could guess where he was going

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who takes the first try at the contest?
options: The Sun
The traveller himself
Neither one; they go together
The North Wind

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the traveller do as the North Wind blows harder?
options: He takes his cloak off at once
He wraps his cloak more closely around himself
He runs back the way he came
He asks the Sun for help

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Sun do at first, before shining in full strength?
options: He hides behind a cloud
He asks the North Wind to stop
He beams gently upon the traveller
He waits for the man to sit down

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the traveller finally do once the Sun shines in full strength?
options: He throws his cloak right off
He wraps his cloak tighter than before
He asks the Sun to stop shining
He sits down and refuses to move

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the North Wind's attack fail to remove the cloak?
options: The traveller is too strong for the wind to affect
The cloak is tied down and cannot be lifted
The North Wind loses interest before finishing
Its force makes the traveller hold the cloak tighter for protection

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the traveller eventually remove his cloak for the Sun?
options: He wants to dry the cloak in the light
The growing warmth makes the cloak uncomfortable to wear
He is following the North Wind's advice
He is copying what other travellers have done

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the North Wind tried to "wrest" the cloak from the man?
options: To fold it neatly for him
To warm it before returning it
To pull it away from him by force
To ask politely if he could borrow it

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: Gentle persuasion can succeed where force fails
The strongest force always wins a contest
Travellers should never wear cloaks in windy weather
The Sun and the North Wind should never compete

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the North Wind approach the traveller?
options: Circling slowly around him
Blowing gently at first
Waiting until he sits down
Whirling furiously down upon him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the traveller do once the Sun first beams gently on him?
options: He wraps his cloak tighter around himself
He unclasps his cloak and lets it hang loosely
He falls asleep in the warmth
He begins to run down the road

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what had the North Wind and the Sun been disputing about before the contest?
options: Which of them the traveller feared more
Which of them could be seen from farther away
Which of them was stronger than the other
Which of them had existed for longer

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the traveller's changing behavior across the contest show?
options: People often resist force but respond to gentleness
People always keep their cloaks on no matter what
The traveller could not decide what to wear
The traveller disliked both the wind and the sun

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Sun's approach be described as gradual rather than sudden?
options: He shines at full strength from the very first moment
He waits for the North Wind to finish before starting
He asks the traveller for permission before beginning
He starts by beaming gently before shining in full strength

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "clad" mean in the phrase "more lightly clad"?
options: Walking at a steady pace
Dressed or covered in clothing
Feeling the warmth of the sun
Standing still in one place

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The North Wind and the Sun both fail to move the traveller
The traveller removes his cloak to help the North Wind win
The Sun succeeds where the North Wind's force had failed
The Sun and the North Wind decide to call off their contest
